title: Decision tree and self-serve surface for air-gapped upgrade requests
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Background: Enterprise customers request air-gapped/on-prem upgrades or network changes frequently; current intake is manual-heavy and inconsistent. This ticket scopes a decision tree and a self-serve intake surface that automates preflight checks, surfaces risk tiers, and routes high-risk requests to the appropriate remediation lane. Goal is to reduce manual triage time, standardize communications, and accelerate low-risk upgrades to a self-service path.
acceptance_criteria: A publishable decision tree diagram (PNG + confluence page) that maps customer responses to one of four outcome lanes: Self-serve auto-approved, Guided self-serve, Standard PM handoff, Enterprise engineering remediation.
A working intake form prototype (Console + shareable link) with conditional fields and embedded network preflight probes that returns a deterministic risk tier in under 90s for 80% of submissions.
Automated routing rules configured in Linear/ServiceDesk so requests labeled 'auto-approve' skip human triage and produce a canned onboarding checklist for the customer.
Playbook snippets and communication templates for each lane (approval, denial with remediation steps, escalation to Dedicated team).
Telemetry events defined: intake_submitted, preflight_pass, tier_assigned, routed_to_team, self_serve_completed.
success_metrics: Reduce average manual triage time from 3.2 hours to <= 30 minutes for incoming private/VPC upgrade requests.
>= 40% of low-risk airgap upgrade requests complete via self-serve within 7 days of submission.
Fewer than 5% of auto-approved requests require rollback or manual intervention within 30 days.
CSAT for private deployment onboarding improves by 10 points in targeted customers in Q2.
proposed_flow: Step 1: Customer fills the intake form (network topology, proxy/firewall config, allowed egress CIDRs, maintenance window constraints, KMS/HSM details).
Step 2: Embedded preflight runs lightweight probes (DNS resolution checks, IP reachability hints, cert chain presence checks) and returns pass/warn/fail codes.
Step 3: Decision tree evaluates responses + preflight signals and assigns a risk tier (A: self-serve, B: guided, C: PM handoff, D: eng remediation).

Step 4: Routing: A->auto-approve path with checklist; B->kickoff with SE-guided session template; C->PM creates scoped intake with required artifacts; D->creates engineering incident/epic with escalation tag.
Step 5: Post-action: automated follow-ups + telemetry capture and customer satisfaction pulse.
intake_form_fields: Current runtime version and desired upgrade target
Onsite engineer contact and escalation contacts
Do you have an approved change window and rollback plan? (Y/N)
Upload: network diagrams, firewall rules export, sysadmin runbook (optional)
Consent checkbox for automated preflight probes
triage_rules: Auto-approve (tier A): preflight_pass && no custom proxy && requested patch is minor patch (same minor version) && maintenance window provided.
Guided (tier B): preflight_warn OR presence of 3rd party proxy OR minor version upgrade with custom KMS; requires SE session within 3 business days.
PM handoff (tier C): major version upgrade OR missing rollback plan OR missing critical artifacts; PM to scope and collect missing info.
Engineering remediation (tier D): preflight_fail OR complex air-gapped network requiring physical IM or on-site support; create ENG epic and SLA target.
routing_and_escalation: Tier A -> automated email + console checklist + 'self-serve ticket' closed after successful completion.
Tier B -> create Linear ticket assigned to Solutions Engineering queue (label: SE-guided) with 3-day SLA.
Tier C -> PM receives intake (label: PM-review) for scoping; schedule discovery within 5 business days.
Tier D -> create ENG-incident epic and tag 'private-onprem-remediation'; designate on-call owner and target 7-day remediation runway.
Escalation if customer marks 'business-critical' or missing artifacts after 10 days -> auto-escalate to GTM lead.
